definition: In machine learning, semantic analysis of a text corpus is the task of building structures that approximate concepts from a large set of documents.
details: It generally does not involve prior semantic understanding of the documents. Semantic analysis strategies include: Metalanguages based on first-order logic, which can analyze the speech of humans. Understanding the semantics of a text is symbol grounding: if language is grounded, it is equal to recognizing a machine-readable meaning. For the restricted domain of spatial analysis, a computer-based language understanding system was demonstrated. Latent semantic analysis (LSA), a class of techniques where documents are represented as vectors in a term space. A prominent example is probabilistic latent semantic analysis (PLSA). Latent Dirichlet allocation, which involves attributing document terms to topics. n-grams and hidden Markov models, which work by representing the term stream as a Markov chain, in which each term is derived from preceding terms.

explainer.lead: In machine learning, semantic analysis of a text corpus builds structures that approximate concepts across a large set of documents, generally without prior semantic understanding of those documents. It matters because it lets concepts emerge from large corpora rather than hand-built meaning.

tiers.eli5: Like reading thousands of documents and building a rough map of what topics keep appearing together, without anyone telling you what they mean first.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply techniques such as latent semantic analysis to derive concept structures from document collections. A pitfall is that these structures approximate concepts without grounded understanding of the documents.
tiers.paperLevel: The task is building structures that approximate concepts from a large document set, generally without prior semantic understanding. Strategies include metalanguages based on first-order logic and latent semantic analysis (LSA), a class of technique. Full semantics involves symbol grounding; for the restricted domain of spatial analysis, a computer-based language understanding system was demonstrated.

explainer.example: LSA is applied to a corpus to derive structures approximating its concepts, without prior semantic understanding of the documents.
